watchlist.thesis: Arqit is a UK-based post-quantum/quantum-safe encryption vendor with real government and satellite-security partnerships (Es'hailSat/AIEE demo), but the stock lacks every pillar of the 'quiet accumulation' pattern: zero open-market insider cash buying in three months of Form 4 filings, institutional flows dominated by passive ETF/index rebalancing rather than active conviction buying (with at least one active manager, Renaissance Technologies, exiting entirely), and a technical picture defined by a violent, still-unexplained single-day crash followed by a fading-volume bounce rather than a gradual base-and-breakout. The rebound off the Sept 14 low is real but reflects mean reversion, not a fresh accumulation signal.
watchlist.risks: The Sept 14 crash (-18.75% on 6-8x average volume) remains completely unexplained after 6+ consecutive research passes across IR, SEC/EDGAR, and news sources — this is now a standing data gap rather than a resolved event, and the absence of an identified negative catalyst is not the same as confirmation nothing is wrong. High historical short interest (~30-37% of float) amplifies volatility in both directions. Single-analyst coverage (HC Wainwright only) with a stale Oct 2025 price target provides very little independent validation. No insider has bought with personal cash at any point in the trailing quarter, which is a disqualifying absence under this screen's core thesis.

news.headline: $464.8 million U.S. Army Enduring-High Energy Laser (E-HEL) contract announced Sept 2, 2026 — the first-ever U.S. production contract for directed-energy (laser) counter-drone systems, covering LOCUST X3 laser weapon deliveries over multiple years. Confirmed via AeroVironment's own investor-relations release and corroborated by multiple financial outlets. Sources: https://investor.avinc.com/news-events/press-releases and https://www.securities.io/aerovironment-wins-464-8-million-army-enduring-high-energy-laser-contract/

Q1 FY2027 earnings call (Sept 9, 2026) disclosed a cluster of additional recent contract wins layered on top of E-HEL: a $500M sole-source IDIQ for the Titan RF detect-and-defeat platform (JIATF-401 Domestic Shield, including an $80M initial order tied to the Golden Dome initiative), a $117.3M Army P550 eVTOL production award, a $51M Switchblade 600 order, a $30M Puma order for Germany's LARUS program, and the first international commercial sale of the LOCUST laser system. Source: AeroVironment Q1 2027 earnings call transcript, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/10/aerovironment-avav-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/

FDA approval (announced 2026-09-04, per Guardant IR and FDA.gov; recirculated by secondary outlets on 2026-09-17-18) of Guardant360 CDx as the first FDA-approved liquid biopsy companion diagnostic for longitudinal ctDNA testing in advanced HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, supported by SERENA-6 trial data. Not a new-today event — dated two weeks prior to this run.

Shield blood test added to EviCore by Evernorth clinical guidelines effective Jan 1, 2027 — announced 2026-09-14 per Guardant IR (also recirculated by SimplyWall.st on 2026-09-17), extending colorectal-cancer screening coverage to an estimated ~94 million additional US adults 45+. Not new-today; dated three days prior to this run.

Announced 2026-09-17: Capricor will present late-breaking HOPE-3 and HOPE-3 open-label extension (OLE) deramiocel (CAP-1002) data — covering skeletal muscle and cardiac outcomes through 24 months, plus delayed-start and natural history analyses — at the 31st Annual Congress of the World Muscle Society (WMS 2026), Hiroshima, Japan, Sept 29-Oct 3, 2026. These analyses were included in a recent major amendment to the Deramiocel BLA.
Deramiocel BLA PDUFA target action date confirmed as November 22, 2026 — the key near-term binary catalyst.

NEW: Syntec Optics announced Sept 10, 2026 that it secured $5 million in additional recurring defense purchase orders, more than doubling its cumulative order book to over $9 million for optics supporting diverse U.S. defense platforms. Cross-verified via the company's own investor-relations site and two independent outlets. Sources: https://syntecoptics.com/investors/ (dated 09/10/2026), https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/syntec-optics-nasdaq-optx-secures-115300840.html, and https://www.globenewswire.com (original wire republished at https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20646535-syntec-optics-nasdaq-optx-secures-5m-additional-recurring-orders-for-diverse-range-of-u-s).

This follows a pattern of recurring, smaller defense/space optics order wins earlier in the year (April $2M AI/AR camera order, July $ unspecified AR display-window orders, Aug 26 space-satellite waveguide order) — the Sept 10 order is the largest and most recent in this cadence, reinforcing (not initiating) the existing order-momentum thesis.

Unusual Machines invested an additional $20 million in XTEND AI Robotics (NYSE:XTND) on Sept 9, 2026, bringing its total investment in XTEND to $27.5 million as part of a larger $110M financing tied to XTEND's business combination and NYSE listing. This catalyst is now over a week old (not new-today) but had not previously been reflected in this ticker's research file; presented here with its correct Sept 9-10, 2026 dating. Cross-verified via two independent sources: the company's own press release (https://www.unusualmachines.com/press-release/) and Streetwise Reports, dated 09/10/2026 (https://www.streetwisereports.com/pub/co/unusual-machines-inc).

NEW: Palladyne AI and FANUC America announced a strategic collaboration on Sept 8, 2026 to combine FANUC's industrial robot portfolio with Palladyne AI's Palladyne IQ physical-AI software platform, targeting manufacturing, warehousing, and logistics automation deployment. This is a significant commercial-diversification catalyst beyond Palladyne's existing defense contract base, cross-verified via the company's own investor-relations site (https://investor.palladyneai.com/news-events/press-releases, dated Sept 8, 2026) and Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/palladyne-ai-fanuc-america-collaborate-120450430.html).

U.S. Air Force exercised an additional $2.9 million option on Palladyne's STRATFI contract (bringing total award to $10.6 million) for Palladyne IQ embodied-AI autonomous robotic systems work — this action is dated July 22, 2026, over a month prior to this run and not being presented as new, but provides supporting context for continued defense-program traction. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/PDYN/palladyne-ai-announces-u-s-air-force-exercise-of-additional-2-9-o8g292rbby76.html

FDA partial clinical hold on BHV-7000 (refractory focal epilepsy) remains in effect as of Sept 17-18, 2026. Confirmed hold was imposed 2026-09-04/announced 2026-09-10 (SEC 8-K, Reuters) due to a rodent-metabolite safety signal of uncertain human relevance; pauses new US enrollment (voluntarily extended ex-US) but existing 600+ enrolled patients continue dosing. No resolution or lifting of the hold has occurred as of this run — checked directly, no change from run #28's open-hold status.
Multiple securities-litigation "investigation notice" press releases (e.g., SueWallSt, Sept 11) circulating around the clinical-hold news — law-firm solicitations, not a fundamental catalyst.

FERC Docket EL26-101-000 (Oklo Inc. v. PJM Interconnection, filed Aug 28, 2026) remains unresolved as of Sept 17-18, 2026 — this is the 9th consecutive stall check (runs #21-29). PJM's own requested Sept 14 action deadline passed with no Commission ruling; Phase I of the Cycle 01 interconnection study is still slated to begin Sept 28, 2026 without Oklo's 750 MW Virginia project reinstated. No adverse or favorable ruling has landed, so per established precedent this stall alone is not grounds for a further score change. Sources: PJM's Sept 4 answer opposing reinstatement (https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/documents/ferc/filings/2026/20260904-el26-101-000.pdf), original complaint (https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/documents/ferc/filings/2026/20260828-el26-101-000.pdf), and confirmation of no order as of Sept 17 via Venture Atlas (https://www.ventureatlas.org/company/oklo) and Utility Dive (https://www.utilitydive.com/news/pjm-oklo-advanced-nuclear-ferc-interconnection/829150/).

NEW since run #28: the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R.9340), which passed the House 417-3 on Sept 16, 2026, hit a Senate roadblock on Sept 17 — Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) attempted a unanimous-consent fast-track, but Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-NM) objected, blocking quick Senate passage and offering a competing, tougher GRID Savings Act. This is a modest incremental negative/delay nuance on the data-center-cost-relief narrative that had helped OKLO on Sept 17, not a reversal of the underlying House passage catalyst. Source: Politico (https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/09/17/congress/data-center-bill-falls-amid-democratic-objection-01082461), dated Sept 17, 2026; House passage confirmed via congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/9340/all-info).
